name: Dialog
summary: A modal window that interrupts the user for a required decision or critical information. Use it for short, focused prompts; use a bottom sheet instead when the content is a longer list of choices or benefits from swipe dismissal.

inputs.name: onDismissRequest
inputs.description: Called when the user dismisses the dialog by clicking outside it or pressing back. Not called when the dismiss button is clicked.

inputs.name: confirmButton
inputs.description: The confirming action, typically a text button.

inputs.name: dismissButton
inputs.description: The dismissing action, typically a text button.

inputs.name: icon
inputs.description: A small hero icon centered above the headline.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The surface the dialog sits on.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: A small hero icon above the headline.

anatomy.name: Actions
anatomy.description: A confirm button and an optional dismiss button.

variants.description: Headline, supporting text and actions, with no icon.
Adds a centered hero icon above the headline. Both variants are the same composable; the difference is purely whether an icon slot is supplied, not a separate shape or size.

layout.text: Width is clamped between 280dp and 560dp; there is no upper bound on height.
Container padding is 24dp on all sides.
The icon, when present, is centered horizontally with 16dp bottom padding, and re-centers the headline under it instead of left-aligning it.
The headline has 16dp bottom padding. Supporting text has 24dp bottom padding and grows to fit its content without being forced to fill remaining space.

There is no built-in max height or scrolling: the content column is not wrapped in a scroll modifier, so long supporting text can overflow the dialog window. An implementor must add scrolling for long content; nothing in Compose clips or truncates it.

Actions sit right-aligned in a wrapping row with 8dp main-axis and 8dp cross-axis spacing. There is no fixed dp breakpoint for wrapping — it wraps whenever the buttons don't fit the available width; the confirm button appears first when stacked and last (trailing) when side-by-side, achieved by flipping layout direction around the row rather than reordering children.

behaviour.text: No press, hover or focus state on the container. Confirm and dismiss slots are ordinary buttons (typically a text button) and own their own interaction states; the dialog's action colour tokens are only a fallback content colour for arbitrary button content — a real text button ignores them and uses its own tokens.
Dismissal happens only through onDismissRequest (outside click or back press) or an explicit button action — there is no swipe-to-dismiss.

No sys.motion.spring.* is referenced anywhere in AlertDialog.kt. The dialog's enter/exit transition comes from the underlying platform dialog window default, not a coded Compose animation. Treat this as an open choice for the target renderer rather than inventing a token that doesn't exist upstream.

keyboard: Escape or a platform back action triggers onDismissRequest.
Tab and Shift+Tab cycle focus between the dismiss button and confirm button (and any focusable dialog content); focus is trapped within the dialog while it is open.
Enter or Space activates the focused button.
semantics: The dialog exposes a pane title ("Dialog") so screen readers announce it as a dialog on entry.
Confirm and dismiss are real buttons; standard minimum touch target applies to both regardless of their visual, often text-only, size.
Headline and supporting text are read as ordinary text content, with no extra live-region behaviour beyond the pane title.

notes.text: MDC-Android's anatomy also lists an optional divider between supporting text and actions; Compose's AlertDialogContent does not render one. Don't assume parity with the View-based divider there.

comp.dialog.container-elevation (level 3) is not actually wired to any shadow or tonal elevation in AlertDialogContent's Surface call — tonalElevation defaults to a hardcoded 0dp and shadowElevation isn't passed at all. Applying a real level-3 shadow is a renderer decision the token alone doesn't enforce in the reference implementation.
"Full-screen dialog" is a separate MDC-Android variant with no Compose equivalent surfaced here — out of scope for this spec.
